messages:
Ashwin: quick sync — proposing a small refactor: introduce a 'safepath' arbitration layer that short-circuits to a stable variant when tail latency or error-rate crosses a threshold. goal: fewer cascading rollbacks, faster automatic recovery. thoughts?
Devin: sounds useful. how strictly do we define 'stable variant'? single pinned model or a decaying candidate set?
Ashwin: prefer single pinned fallback per route for predictability. fallback config could be: {fallback_model: v1.9, trigger_window_ms: 5000, spike_factor: 3, min_sample: 50} (proto).
Maria: +1 for pinned. also we need to ensure stateful sessions are respected — don't flip mid-session unless eviction is allowed.
Jules: what about canaries that intentionally increase latency for quality? will safepath always win and mask that signal?
Ashwin: good point. idea: safepath applies only after a 'probe isolation' check: if canary traffic ratio < probe_threshold OR probe signals failed, then short-circuit. otherwise let canary run for its planned window.
Devin: can we express this as a small state machine? Healthy -> Observing -> Spike -> ShortCircuited. transitions based on error_rate & p95 latency + sample count.
Kevin: ops concern: need observability hooks and an explicit audit event when safepath triggers. otherwise oncall will see only 'traffic dropped to v1.9' and get confused.
OpsBot: [auto] safepath trigger detected for route /gen/chat at 1749123468. reason: p95 1250ms > threshold 400ms, sample 120.
Maria: +1 on audit. also add a cooldown: once safepath engages, keep it for min_cooldown_ms or until manual clear to avoid flip-flop.
Jules: What about multi-variant fallbacks? e.g., fall back to lighter quantized variant instead of the older model to preserve quality.
Ashwin: support for variant prioritization is planned: fallback list with priority tags (stable, light, degraded). safepath picks highest-priority available.
Devin: API-wise, how do we expose this to product teams? simple flags in rollout spec? example:
```
rollout: {canary: 5%, safepath: {enabled: true, fallback: [v1.9, v1.8-quant], cooldown_ms: 300000}}
```
Kevin: add a 'reason_hint' and 'signal_snapshot' to the safepath event so SRE can triage quickly.
Jules: one more: ensure session affinity mapping persists to fallback when sessions carry state (e.g., chat history). otherwise we create context mismatch.
Ashwin: plan: safepath will call the router to remap affinity to chosen fallback instance group, and emit a mapping delta event. sessions with KV caches will get a cache-warmup probe if >staleness_window.
Maria: edge case: what if fallback is out of capacity? should we have a degraded-mode that partial-serves (token limits) instead of full short-circuit?
Devin: propose fallback policy with three outcomes: full-switch, degrade-grace (throttle tokens / reduce max_len), and reject-to-legacy. choose based on capacity signal + signal severity score.
Ashwin: agreed. next steps: I'll draft a tiny RFC with state machine, rollout spec example, safepath event schema, and a short runbook for oncall. want reviewers: @Devin, @Maria, @Jules, @Kevin.
Jules: happy to review. please include failure-mode diagrams.
Kevin: +1 - also include metric names and dashboard widgets.
OpsBot: [reminder] RFC draft PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/rfcs/pulls/789 — reviewers requested: Devin, Maria, Jules, Kevin.
Ashwin: thanks — will ping once PR is up for review. :thumbsup:
Devin: ack.
Maria: ack.
Jules: ack.
Kevin: ack.
